transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's nice to meet you too. Um, thank you for seeing me. I... I guess I'm here because I've been having a little trouble lately. It's probably nothing major, but I just wanted to make sure everything is okay. 

I've just been noticing that I'm forgetting little things that I normally handle fine. You know, just silly things, like... I'll forget to return a phone call, or I won't turn in a registration form on time, or I'll completely forget to stop and run an errand on my way home from work. It's a little embarrassing to even bring it up, honestly. I feel like I should just be able to keep track of these things, you know? Does that make sense? I just thought it might be good to talk to someone about it.
Did you have trouble with attention or forgetfulness like this when you were a child?

Um, well... I guess, looking back, maybe a little bit? I mean, I wasn't a bad student or anything, I promise. I always tried really hard to do what I was told. 

But... yeah, even back in elementary school, I guess I was kind of that kid who would forget to bring home permission slips, or I'd somehow lose my finished homework right there at the bottom of my backpack. It's a little embarrassing to admit, honestly. And for things like bigger projects, my mom or my teachers usually had to, um, sort of remind me step by step to actually finish them. I just thought all kids were a little scatterbrained sometimes, you know? Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do these forgetfulness and attention problems cause trouble for you in more than one part of your life, like both at work and at home?

Oh, um... I wouldn't really use the word trouble. I certainly try not to let it affect anyone else, I promise. I work as an administrative assistant, so... well, my whole job is keeping things organized for other people. I really, really try my best there, and I don't think my boss has noticed anything bad. I just have to, um, maybe double-check my sticky notes a lot more than other people might have to, just to be safe. 

And at home... I guess that's where I let things slip a little more, like those errands I mentioned earlier. But it's not like my whole life is falling apart or anything! I usually manage to keep it together pretty well overall. Does that answer your question? I just really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or making excuses.
Have these forgetfulness problems caused you to make a significant mistake at work?

Oh, no, definitely no significant mistakes! I promise I'm very careful about the big things. I'm still getting by just fine, really. 

But... well, I guess I have missed a few small work follow-ups here and there. And, um, some school deadlines, too. It's nothing catastrophic, I swear! It's just... it's happened often enough lately that I do worry a little bit. I'm really hoping to move into an Office Manager role eventually, and I'm just so scared that these little slip-ups might start to affect my reputation. I want everyone to know they can completely rely on me. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm doing a bad job, because I really do try my absolute best. Does that make sense?
Do you often have trouble staying focused on a task, even when you want to pay attention?

Um, well... I don't think I have a huge problem with that, really. I mean, if it's something important, I can usually force myself to sit down and just get it done. I really try to be a good listener and stay on top of things. 

Sometimes, maybe, if a task is really long or, um, a bit repetitive, my mind might wander just a tiny bit? But I think that happens to everyone, right? I always catch myself and get right back to work. I wouldn't say I *often* have trouble, just... maybe occasionally, like anyone else. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just don't want you to think I'm slacking off or anything.
Did these memory problems start after a particularly stressful event or period in your life?

Oh, um... I wouldn't really call it a stressful event, exactly. I don't want to sound ungrateful or anything, because it's actually a really good thing! But... well, I did start an evening certificate program about 15 months ago. 

And I guess... maybe since then, these little attention and organization things have been noticeably harder to manage. Just because my plate is a little fuller, you know? It's definitely not that I can't handle it, I promise! It's just been a bit more of a juggling act since I added classes on top of my normal work schedule, so the slip-ups might be a tiny bit more obvious now. Is that the kind of thing you were looking for? I hope I'm answering these right.
Compared with how you were a few years ago, do you feel your memory is actually getting worse?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say it's getting *worse*, exactly! I mean, I really don't feel like I'm losing my memory or anything scary like that. I think my brain still works just fine. 

It's really just... well, like I mentioned, I just have a lot more on my plate now with the certificate program and work. So I think it's more about having too many things to keep track of, rather than my memory actually failing me, if that makes sense? I'm still the same person I was a few years ago, just... maybe a little busier. I hope that doesn't sound like I'm making excuses! Does that sound normal to you?
Do you often feel anxious or worried?

Um, anxious? No, I don't think so. I mean, I wouldn't say I'm a worrier or anything like that. 

I try to stay really positive and just, you know, take things as they come. Sometimes I might get a little bit stressed if I have a big deadline at work or a test coming up for my classes, but I think that's just normal stress, right? Not like... clinical anxiety or anything. I always try to keep a smile on and push through it. I hope that's okay? I just really try not to let things get to me too much.
When you were a child, did your forgetfulness or disorganization cause problems at home?

Oh, um... well, I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I really don't want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or anything, because I always tried my best! I was a good kid, I promise. 

But, um, I suppose even back in elementary school, I was kind of... that kid. You know, the one who would forget to bring permission slips home, or I'd do my homework and then somehow it would just disappear into the bottom of my backpack. And, um, my mom or my teachers would usually have to kind of... sit with me and remind me step by step to actually finish my projects. 

It wasn't that I didn't want to do the work! I just... got a little sidetracked sometimes. I think a lot of kids are like that though, right? Just a little scatterbrained when they're young? I hope that doesn't make me sound terrible. Is that the kind of thing you meant?
Do you often put off starting tasks that require a lot of mental effort, like paperwork or school assignments?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say I *put things off* exactly. I mean, I really try to stay on top of everything! I always want to do a good job. 

But I guess... maybe sometimes, if it's something that takes a lot of focus? Like, if an assignment for my certificate program means I have to sit down and read a really long chapter, or if I have to write out a whole detailed plan... I might, um, find other things to do first? 

It's just because I want to make sure I have enough time to do it right! But then, sometimes, I end up waiting until it's a bit late, and I have to kind of rush through it after work when I'm already tired. I always get it done, though! I promise I'm not lazy or anything. I just... maybe I don't always manage my time perfectly when it's a really heavy task. Does that make sense? I hope that's an okay answer.
At home, do these attention or organization problems often cause you to miss important tasks or responsibilities?

Oh, um... at home? Well, I mean, I really try to keep things running smoothly. I don't want you to think everything is falling apart or anything, because I'm definitely still getting by! I manage to keep the lights on and all that.

But, um... I guess maybe there are a few little things that slip through the cracks sometimes? Like, occasionally I might forget to pay a small bill right on time, or I'll mean to do a chore and just... forget. And, well, I guess sometimes it bleeds over a little bit into other things? Like, I've missed a couple of small follow-ups at work, or maybe a minor deadline for my certificate classes. 

It's nothing huge! I always apologize and fix it right away. But I do worry a little bit, just because... well, I really want to move up to an Office Manager role eventually, and I'd hate for people to think I'm not reliable. I really am reliable, I promise! I just get a little overwhelmed sometimes. Is that... is that the kind of thing you're asking about? I hope I'm explaining this right.
